messages:
sre-oncall: seeing a user error tied to request_id=abc12345 and trace_id=4f2a9b6c7d. anyone know the easiest way to pull the full logs/traces for that id? need both console link and cli option.

aj: easiest is Console -> Logs and search by request_id. Quick direct link (replace id): https://console.redwood.ai/logs?query=request_id%3Aabc12345&from=2026-03-16T07%3A00%3A00Z&to=2026-03-16T09%3A00%3A00Z :eyes:

todd: CLI: use redwoodctl (installed on oncall image)
```
redwoodctl logs query --request-id abc12345 \
  --start 2026-03-16T07:00:00Z --end 2026-03-16T09:00:00Z \
  --format json --include-trace
```
that returns matching log events and a trace_id field when available. add `--follow` for streaming recent logs.

maria: if you already have trace_id you can jump to the trace UI: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/4f2a9b6c7d (replace with full hex). For API access (scriptable):
```
curl -s "https://tracing.redwood.ai/api/trace/4f2a9b6c7d" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRACING_API_KEY" | jq
```
this gives spans + timestamps so you can correlate to logs.

infra-bot: logs are indexed under field `request_id` and `request.id`. Retention: logs 30d, traces 7d (sampling default 1%). To pull archived logs contact infra.

aj: note: some long-running async jobs only write job_id instead of request_id. if you suspect that, search job_id:<id> or use /jobs endpoint. also we standardize header X-Request-Id -> request_id field; if upstream didn't set it you might get a generated id in `request.generated_id`.

maria: if you want I can run the redwoodctl query for abc12345 and paste a compact result here — tell me the time window you want me to search. :+1:

sre-oncall: please run 07:30-08:30 UTC, thanks. will also try the console link.

aj: small tip for alert tuning: if you want a pager on 5xxs for specific route, create log-based alert in Console -> Alerts with query `status_code:[500 TO 599] AND route:\"/v1/generate\"` and set burn-in to 5min to reduce flaps.

sre-oncall: perfect, thanks all. pinging here so anyone else can follow the steps later. :white_check_mark:
